forecasts.label: Interest payable

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Combined Authority's auditor expects a qualified 2025/26 accounts opinion
news_drafts.lead:
The Combined Authority's external auditor, the accountancy firm EY, expects to issue a qualified opinion on its 2025/26 accounts, meaning it could not fully sign them off. The audit results report put to the Audit and Governance Committee on 12 November says the audit is substantially complete, subject to outstanding procedures. It would be the first audit opinion the Authority has received since 2022/23. The auditor disclaimed its opinion, declining to give one, for both 2023/24 and 2024/25.

The Authority's covering report says the qualification arises from national audit backstop issues, not from errors identified in the accounts. The auditor could not gain assurance over the 2022/23 closing balances, which carry forward into later years. In the report's words, "This opinion is qualified only due to the impact of carried forward balances lacking assurance as a result of the national audit issues identified earlier." The auditor also says it does not currently expect its report to refer to any material uncertainty about the Authority's ability to continue preparing its accounts as an ongoing organisation.

The auditor's draft report anticipates another qualified opinion for 2026/27, as assurance improves, and says an unqualified opinion is possible for 2027/28. The Combined Authority says it wants to discuss with the auditors whether unqualified opinions could return earlier.

news_drafts.headline: Cambridgeshire and Peterborough transport spending is £7.7m so far, against a £10.2m year-to-date budget
news_drafts.lead:
Day-to-day spending on transport at the Cambridgeshire and Peterborough combined authority stands at £7.7m for the year to date, against a year-to-date budget of £10.2m, an underspend of £2.5m. The figures are in the Budget and Performance Report going to the Transport Committee on 4 November.

The report says most of the year-to-date underspend sits in public transport bus services. In its words, "the underspend here is because of a lag in billing from contractors". The report does not present the year-to-date gap as a saving for the year.

The full-year budget for transport is £23.8m and the full-year forecast is £23.7m, a variance of £125k below budget. The report gives a separate reason for that forecast variance: the start of the Market Towns Cycle Support scheme has been delayed and its spending is now spread over three years.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Performance against Treasury Management and Capital Indicators and Limits
findings.headline: Bus franchising capital expenditure of £18.71m is forecast to be debt-financed by 31 March 2027, with no debt-funded spend recorded to 30 September 2026.
findings.detail: The capital financing requirement is forecast at £19.12m at 31 March 2027. The authorised limit for external debt is £84.61m and the operational boundary is £74.61m, with actual debt of £0.47m at 30 September 2026, which is the Pathfinder House lease. The capital financing table records debt of 0 for 2026/27.
findings.matters: A finance director would want to know when debt will be needed to fund a major transport scheme, and how it squares with the authorised limit and the zero debt figure in the financing table.
findings.figures: Bus Franchising debt-funded capex forecast: £18.71m at 31.3.2027; CFR forecast £19.12m; authorised limit £84.61m; operational boundary £74.61m; actual debt £0.47m at 30.9.26.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Performance against Treasury Management and Capital Indicators and Limits
findings.headline: Capital expenditure was £36m at 30 September 2026 against a 2026/27 budget of £107m, up from £11m at 30 June 2026.
findings.detail: General Fund capital spend was £34m and capital investments £2m at 30 September 2026. The paper gives no year-to-date forecast or variance commentary for the capital programme.
findings.matters: A finance director at this council or a peer would compare six-month capital spend against the annual budget to judge whether the programme is on track.
findings.figures: Budget as at 30.9.26: £107m total (General Fund £102m; capital investments £5m). Actual to 30.6.26: £11m. Actual to 30.9.26: £36m (General Fund £34m; capital investments £2m).

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Performance against Treasury Management and Capital Indicators and Limits
findings.headline: The lender's option to exit on two three-year fixed-rate deals has been activated, with both loans due for repayment in Qtr3 2026/27.
findings.detail: The paper says the authority agreed two three-year fixed-rate deals with an annual lender's option to exit, which are excluded from the principal limits. Long-term principal invested beyond year end was £35m at 30 June 2026 and £55m at 30 September 2026, against a 2026/27 limit of £80m. The paper does not give the rates, the replacement funding cost or the counterparty's name.
findings.matters: An early exit by the counterparty means cash returns to the authority sooner than the original term, and a finance director would need to know how the replacement funding is arranged.
findings.figures: Long-term principal beyond year end: £35m at 30.6.26; £55m at 30.9.26; limit for 2026/27 £80m.
findings.quote: The option has been activated and both loans are now due

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Performance against Treasury Management and Capital Indicators and Limits
findings.headline: Treasury investments were £213.5m at 30 September 2026, down from £229.8m at 30 June 2026, and are forecast at £50.9m at 31 March 2027.
findings.detail: The paper reports zero outstanding external borrowing at each date and says the Combined Authority had no immediate plans for external borrowing in 2026/27. It states that treasury investments are held at a minimum of £10m to manage day-to-day cash flow.
findings.matters: A finance director would want to see how far the authority expects its cash balances to run down over the year, and that it is not planning to borrow to replace them.
findings.figures: Treasury investments: £229.8m actual at 30.6.26; £213.5m actual at 30.9.26; £50.9m forecast at 31.3.2027. Minimum cash balance: £10m.

findings.paper_title: Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Combined Authority Audit Results Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Auditor does not currently expect a material uncertainty related to going concern to be referred to in its report.
findings.detail: The auditor says it has not identified events that would cast significant doubt on the Authority's ability to prepare accounts on a going concern basis. It notes that financial sustainability matters do not themselves indicate a material uncertainty where statutory services continue.
findings.matters: A finance director at a council facing financial sustainability questions will look at how the auditor distinguishes sustainability concerns from going concern uncertainty.
findings.quote: We do not currently expect our auditor’s report to include any reference to a material uncertainty related to going concern.
